problem_title: Nonconvergence of randomized subtraction games with all odd moves

evidence.text:
For every finite nonempty set of positive odd subtraction moves, with uniform choice among the legal moves, the probability of winning for the player to move does not converge as the heap grows. A positive finite-window invariant proves the result without a coprimality or root-simplicity assumption. This answers the separate all-odd nonconvergence assertion in Capitelli and Somma; the different MathDB root-simplicity conjecture is not resolved.See full solutionHide full solutionAI-assisted preprint by Myeongjin Kang, with no affiliation.
